# Warm Blob verification worker experiment

2026-09-13. **First candidate rejected on combined memory; one bounded follow-up is authorized for design/implementation/review/measurement only.** Shipped adapter 0.5.2 and its original app loading budget remain the acceptance control. Required follow-up sequence: Astra medium specification → Luna xhigh implementation → fresh Astra medium verification → Root measurement, with memory first. The original design and historical review requirements below remain binding except where the self-contained “Consumed warm-worker read-buffer disposal” amendment explicitly changes disposal, private capability eligibility and measurement order. ## Candidate and scope

One preparation-owned pool of asynchronous Blob-reading/full-BLAKE3 workers, lazily instantiated, maximum `min(2, admitted source concurrency, funded warm slots)`. A worker runs one complete warm source at a time and is reused only within that preparation. Keep interval-local 512 KiB reads, ordered 64 KiB zero updates and real MessageChannel task checkpoints including every nonempty gap's final block. No FileReaderSync, synchronous OPFS handles, read-ahead, packed payload reads, zero batching, width sweep, metadata lookup optimization, persistent global pool, or public performance knob.

Changes are adapter loading plus one app loading-budget expression and package integration. Engine 0.2.4, codec 0.1.1, audio, feed, pump, engine initialization and playback remain fixed. Full canonical BLAKE3 and exact byte counts still precede readiness. Historical qualified MessageChannel512 ready median is 1824.3 ms, not a promise for the newly frozen control. About 518 ms of hash CPU means ideal two-way hash division alone cannot demonstrate the remaining 824 ms to sub-second ready.

Root reports released main `e8b119cc013b205be18f5273bd66ece944b787ad`, completed app adoption PR 211 at `f10b304d326f8677e636c3188ce7fe9e6cc2f780`, and deployment run `34770127132` live. The next clean implementation worktree is `/tmp/miso-warm-worker-adapter`, branch `perf/warm-blob-workers`, at that released adapter main; dependency installation is Root-owned. These delivery facts are Root reports, not independently rerun by this design. The inspected worktree `/tmp/miso-task-yield-adapter` remains `f5348e1eecf1bad150ec17d73c1ee891cb47a35f`, version 0.5.2. Root must verify release/inspected-source correspondence and freeze the adopted app/package/harness hashes before implementation/measurement.

## Resolve the real mixed warm/cold reservation seam

Current `sparse-store.ts:438–500` uses registered `scheduling.concurrency` for `Effect.forEach(prepareUnique)`. That bounds simultaneous source tasks, warm and cold together. `sparse-scheduling.ts` exposes only this number and the retained FLAC pool. Warm `installSource` does not acquire the FLAC admission. `FlacWorkerPool` owns a separate physical admission and can keep idle decoder workers and their reservations until the preparation epoch closes. Thus “warm jobs use existing 8 MiB reservations” is false; warm workers cannot borrow those idle reservations without changing the retained pool.

Use **explicit unused memory-budget headroom**, not a FLAC pool redesign:

- For an otherwise eligible native resolver without caller-owned `admission`, let `C = widths.processing`, and `B = snapshot.memoryBudgetBytes ?? defaultFlacMemoryBudgetBytes(resolvedDeviceMemory)`. Resolve the same browser hint/default semantics as the existing width computation; no second inconsistent device read. Compute `K = min(2, C, floor(max(0, B - C * FLAC_WORKER_RESERVATION_BYTES) / W))`, with `W = 2 MiB` per warm slot. Safe integer validation is mandatory. `K = 0` retains baseline verification.
- `sparse-resolver.ts` registers a private `tryClaimWarmPreparation()` capability alongside concurrency/pool. One synchronous resolver-local occupied flag grants at most one preparation claim at a time, with immutable `width: K` and idempotent release. No queue, workers, or Blob references live in this registration. A concurrent preparation that cannot claim uses baseline verification; it does not wait, spawn an extra pool or bypass the shared budget. The claim is released only after its preparation pool has been terminated. This preserves the existing resolver-wide FLAC pool capacity even across overlapping preparations.
- `openSession` acquires that claim in its existing preparation scope and lazily owns the warm pool there. Its existing `forEach` concurrency stays `C`. Warm queue entries are already admitted source tasks; cold misses take the unchanged resolver/FLAC route and never occupy warm slots. Keep all retained FLAC scopes/finalizers intact. Physical resources may now reach `C` retained cold workers plus `K` warm workers, explicitly charged as `C * 8 MiB + K * 2 MiB <= B`. The warm pool never represents itself as a FLAC reservation.
- Initial eligibility excludes any caller-owned `admission`, explicit `createWorker`, or explicit `assets` object. Standalone `openSource`/`installSource`, wrapped/custom/unregistered resolvers, and sessions without a resolver remain on the accepted main-realm verifier. This conservatively preserves deployment and shared-admission behavior. It does not assert that the historical standalone warm path acquired caller admission.
- The current app passes `memoryBudgetBytes: concurrency * 8 MiB`, which leaves no warm headroom when its requested width is realized. The candidate app loading expression in `src/lib/mixer/engine/open-session.ts` must become `concurrency * 8 MiB + 4 MiB`, keeping `maximumWorkers: concurrency` and every other option fixed. The primary acceptance comparison keeps the shipped app expression in control A and includes this extra allowance in candidate B. Assert that registered source width is unchanged. This is a reservation increase, not a measured physical-memory claim. Use the existing public `memoryBudgetBytes` option; no new public configuration field, asset override or tuning API is introduced. No UI or catalog changes are needed.

For preferences `n = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16`, the memory-limited width remains `floor((8n + 4)/8) = n`, exactly as `floor(8n/8) = n`; the existing hardware and `maximumWorkers: n` caps still apply. The configured budgets change respectively 8→12, 16→20, 32→36, 64→68, and 128→132 MiB. Hardware may lower actual C in either arm, identically; K remains at most C and two. The current legacy `flacAdmissionWidth` validates a positive safe budget with at least 8 MiB; its automatic-default 32 MiB ceiling is not a ceiling on explicit budgets. Do not add a new public ceiling. The public option remains a conservative package reservation policy, not a guarantee of total browser RSS: allocate the cold capacity it already funds first, then only previously unused explicit/default headroom to eligible warm resources. Existing callers that exhaust their budget get baseline behavior; no caller receives a hidden budget increase. Update the option documentation/comment to state that unused budget may fund native sparse warm verification while cold width remains fixed.

This is the necessary scope choice: a default fully allocated resolver deliberately gets compatibility verification. If Root rejects the explicit additional 4 MiB app allowance, do not implement a hidden additive worker budget or redesign FLAC retention; return for a revised bounded design. The selection did not establish spare reservations.

## Exact implementation boundary

1. `src/stems/sparse-scheduling.ts`: private claim type/capability above, still identity-bound through the existing WeakMap. `src/stems/sparse-resolver.ts`: snapshot eligibility, compute funded slots, own the single preparation claim. Do not edit `flac-worker-pool.ts` or its admission algorithm.
2. `src/stems/sparse-store.ts`: thread a private optional warm context through the internal `installSource` function's extra internal parameter, supplied only by `openSession`; do not add a key to the public options/schema. Refactor `verifyMarker` minimally: perform `admitMarkerMetadata` once under the current identity lock, then select worker or unchanged local verification of that admitted Blob/index. Keep the local helper's MessageChannel cadence. No second metadata read or reopened Blob in either branch.
3. New `src/stems/sparse-verify-worker-pool.ts`: small private Effect-owned pool and bounded callback transport. At most K slot records and C admitted job references; Effect remains responsible for source/control resource lifetime. Use scoped acquisition and callback interruption cleanup, not a replacement application promise scheduler. A small FIFO of already admitted jobs is sufficient. No generic scheduler, public service or priority scheme.
4. New `src/stems/sparse-verify-worker-protocol.ts`: versioned narrow start/progress/ack/complete/failure messages, scalar safe-integer validation, job/generation IDs and fixed metadata bounds. New `src/internal/engine-web-sparse-verify-worker.ts`: Effect-owned verification loop importing only the protocol, BLAKE3 helper and minimal relevant dependencies. Its graph must not initialize codec/FLAC delivery or engine/audio modules.
5. New private factory `src/stems/sparse-verify-worker-asset.ts`: literal `new Worker(new URL('../internal/engine-web-sparse-verify-worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })`. This preserves the package-relative worker pattern without expanding public asset overrides. `scripts/copy-assets.mjs` bundles this self-contained worker entry into `dist/internal`, as it already does the FLAC/OPFS entries. Update `scripts/check-package.mjs` and existing browser packed harness for the asset/import closure. Existing `sideEffects: ['./dist/internal/*.js']` and published `dist` inclusion cover the new file; verify packed output rather than assuming that suffices.
6. Focused tests in `tests/sparse-store.test.ts`, `tests/sparse-resolver.test.ts`, and one new worker transport test file. App change is the single loading-budget expression above plus appropriate verification. No new dependencies.

## Admitted descriptor and bounded wire representation

`admitMarkerMetadata` validates marker/index/expectation and obtains `data`; retain that exact main-realm Blob for the final frozen descriptor, together with the original admitted index. Never reopen a path or accept a worker-returned Blob. Serialize this Blob to the worker: File API serialization carries its byte sequence and snapshot state, but promises neither zero-copy memory nor immunity from later backing-file mutation. [File API](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-section).

Do not structured-clone the object-shaped interval array. For a running slot only, create a packed `Float64Array` containing triples `(startFrame, frames, byteOffset)` from the immutable admitted index and transfer its backing ArrayBuffer with the Blob job. Cap this array at **256 KiB**, hence at most `floor(262144 / 24) = 10922` intervals. Indices above this private eligibility ceiling retain local verification without allocation of the packed copy. This is a compatibility choice, not rejection of a formerly valid source. Pending jobs hold existing admitted objects only; no packed copies, hash instances or payload buffers. The original descriptor metadata remains charged by existing session rules (`512 + 128 * intervalCount`), separate from the new transferred metadata. The 8 MiB encoded-marker limit is not a JavaScript heap bound.

Wire start includes protocol version, slot generation, unique job ID, expected identity/digest and scalar format/count fields, Blob, packed intervals, and configured store read deadline. The worker independently validates ordered safe arithmetic, interval non-overlap, active offsets, frame bounds, packed length, Blob size, and active/canonical totals before reading. All active reads stay interval-local, max 512 KiB; no extra PCM transfers to the main thread. Count actual reads, read bytes, hash updates and canonical bytes in bounded scalar accumulators.

Worker returns digest and exact counts plus the existing verification timing components. Main accepts only a message from the current slot generation/current pending job and validates version, identity, expected active total, exact canonical count and digest against the admitted expectation. Source/aggregate ready remain exclusively on main. All-zero and empty-active valid sources still hash every canonical zero byte. Ghost remains 845 reads, 249,323,400 active bytes, 297,980,304 canonical bytes, 1010 zero checkpoints, eight accepted stems, and no warm stem/FLAC requests.

The worker clears its job Blob/index/hash/current-buffer references and local listeners before posting completion. Completion is the reusable-slot reset acknowledgement; reject any attempted overlapping job. A new job creates fresh mutable hash state. No second reset protocol or retained per-source history is necessary. Main retains the original admitted descriptor until its normal handoff/cleanup.

## Progress, deadlines and cancellation

Each hash update advances the worker's scalar latest progress; zero updates retain the 64 KiB task checkpoint. At most one unacknowledged progress notification and one latest counter exist. Main validates monotonic bytes in `[0, canonicalBytes]`, feeds the existing observer reporter, rechecks abort, and sends one matching acknowledgement. Do not wait for that acknowledgement to hash the next block; it only authorizes the next progress notification. Complete may overtake an acknowledgement but follows already posted progress on the worker channel; it carries terminal progress and supersedes any unsent latest value. Clear protocol state on completion. Do not change observer throttling/throw isolation or treat progress at total as verification proof. Preserve main-side terminal progress flush and abort checks after observers and before descriptor/source-ready; observer-triggered abort must win. Intermediate raw hash events may coalesce at transport; every raw update remains accounted in diagnostic counts.

A worker uses asynchronous `blob.slice(...).arrayBuffer()` with the existing configured per-read deadline. A main-side **no-progress watchdog using the same readDeadlineMs** begins at construction/start and resets only on valid increasing progress or completion, never arbitrary chatter; it bounds a missing startup reply, dead worker or unavailable transport. Worker-side read deadline preserves the read failure distinction. Slow background scheduling may cause the same class of deadline refusal; record target visibility in evidence. No overall short fixed load timeout or per-block heartbeat messages. Map cancellation to existing `SparseCancelledError`, read/watchdog deadline to `SparseDeadlineError`, malformed protocol/digest/count/short-read to `SparseCorruptError`, and worker construction/post/error/messageerror/read I/O to existing appropriate boundary/I/O errors through the store's public mapper. Do not add a decoder error for a hash worker.

Caller abort and store close use the already combined operation signal. Queued cancellation removes its entry and listeners promptly. Running cancellation first invalidates job/generation, detaches handlers/watchdog, terminates that worker and clears references, then settles cancellation. It must not wait for a Blob read, progress ack, worker task or graceful reply. Effect interruption cleanup does the same idempotently. Terminate a failed slot and do not silently retry its source on main. Cleanup precedes that source's identity-lock release. On preparation failure, sibling tasks cancel and all slots terminate; on success all slots terminate before leaving the preparation scope and before aggregate ready. Attempt every cleanup even if one throws; preserve failures and block readiness/claim reuse if termination itself fails.

A normal idle reusable worker has no old source references; successful source cleanup need not terminate that idle slot. Late completion/progress/errors from cancelled jobs or prior worker generations cannot settle a replacement job. A retry uses a fresh slot generation and fresh state. Keep counters bounded safe integers and close the pool on exhaustion rather than wrapping IDs. A worker termination request aborts worker execution/discards tasks, but its void return is not evidence that native memory was physically reclaimed immediately. [HTML worker termination](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/workers.html#terminate-a-worker).

Only predispatch capability/eligibility failures fall back: absent/non-callable Worker or MessageChannel, absent WebAssembly, unfunded/exclusive-claim unavailable, customization/shared policy, oversized packed metadata. A module load/CSP/construction/runtime failure after selecting the worker is a typed failure, not an invisible successful fallback. Record which route ran. Fallback keeps the accepted 0.5.2 verifier and its existing stalled-Blob cancellation limitation; do not claim the worker's prompt termination fixes the compatibility path.

## Memory envelope and evidence

Per funded slot W = 2 MiB conservatively accounts these package-controlled live byte stores:

| Component | Maximum |
| --- | ---: |
| Current Blob ArrayBuffer (no read-ahead) | 512 KiB |
| Zero block | 64 KiB |
| Packed transferred interval metadata | 256 KiB |
| BLAKE3 instance linear memory | 128 KiB, verify against pinned hash-wasm asset |
| Fixed protocol/hash wrapper/control allowance | 64 KiB |
| Remaining reservation headroom | 1024 KiB |

Total named components are 1024 KiB; the remaining 1 MiB is reservation headroom, not proof of browser overhead. Only one payload result is reachable per slot; release it before launching the next read. BLAKE3's internal input copy is inside the counted Wasm memory. Compilation code/module, Blob serialization/backing storage, JS object layout, Effect/runtime/code heaps, GC delay and native worker/OPFS resources are opaque; disclose them separately, never call them zero. Fresh instances from completed jobs may await GC; bounded references are not an instantaneous physical-RSS bound. Ensure the packed worker contains only the used BLAKE3 implementation, not all hash algorithms or a FLAC module loader. If inspection disproves the 128 KiB Wasm figure or the bounded import graph, stop and revise the reservation before measurement, rather than silently consuming headroom.

Root keeps three separate sampled-memory runs per arm and extends existing Chromium target sampling only enough to include attributable worker isolates/heaps/resources, with snapshots before load, peak, after preparation teardown, and matched reopen. Report main and worker contributions separately plus combined observable peak; a lower main heap is not a memory saving. Freeze acceptance now: combined attributable median peak rise must be at most `4 MiB + max(4 MiB, 5% of control combined peak)` (the explicit added reservation plus the prior noise allowance). No rising retained worker count/source references after teardown/reopen. If worker/native attribution is unavailable, record deterministic accounting and exclusions, but treat the combined-memory qualification as missing rather than passing from main-only samples. No general memory profiling framework.

## Meaningful qualification and frozen decision

First prove one compact mixed fixture: two warm and two cold sources under a width-two and sufficiently funded resolver. Hold one cold job until a warm job completes, then retain the cold worker idle while the second warm runs. Assert source tasks never exceed C, warm workers never exceed K, cold physical workers remain within C, and the explicit aggregate reservation formula holds. Include a second simultaneous preparation using the same resolver (baseline fallback), zero-headroom and caller-owned shared admission paths, width one, and exact metadata eligibility boundary. The fixture establishes admission/lifetime behavior, not a new performance corpus.

Integrity fixtures use independent canonical byte/digest oracles for active, silent, mixed, boundary tails and tampered input; compare counts/read calls against baseline. Cover descriptor object identity and a backend that would return different bytes on a second get, proving no reopen. Exercise actual module worker semantics in the existing packed browser lane; fake workers alone cannot qualify Blob serialization or URL delivery.

Transport/lifecycle tests hold startup, Blob read, progress ack and completion separately where relevant. Abort/store close must reject promptly without delivering the withheld event, never ready; allow late stale events and verify a clean retry. Include terminal observer abort, throwing observer, wrong job/generation, mismatched digest/count, worker error, progress queue bound, slot reuse and teardown before aggregate ready/lock release. Use focused representative cases, not an exhaustive timing matrix. Missing progress and read timeout produce typed deadline failures. Construction/post/termination faults must not leak a claim or report ready.

Run adapter `npm run check`, packed fresh-consumer worker loading, and existing actual OPFS Chromium/WebKit lanes. App adoption checks remain lint/typecheck/test/build. Fresh Astra reviews resource ordering, mixed reservation arithmetic, protocol validation, scalar overflow and descriptor binding. Root freezes source/test/package/harness/app hashes. No source-tree-only worker qualification. Physical Safari/iPad correctness/performance remains a distinct unqualified target without actual device evidence.

For the primary ready and memory comparison, A = the actual shipped 0.5.2 MessageChannel512 app with its original `concurrency * 8 MiB` budget; B = reviewed candidate including its additional 4 MiB allowance. Keep source width/order, browser/device, Ghost cache and observers matched and assert identical derived source width. Report the full candidate cost, including the budget increase and worker/native overhead. An optional single equal-headroom control diagnostic may run released 0.5.2 with +4 MiB only to confirm unchanged policy/behavior; it never replaces shipped A in acceptance, creates another performance arm, or supplies favorable substitute rows. Fresh measured navigation creates the pool; no worker prewarm outside the timed load. Retain one unmeasured cache prime per arm. Five alternating pairs **AB, BA, AB, BA, AB**, every row retained. Timing diagnostics/memory run separately.

Use the prior frozen descriptive screen: `d = A.ready - B.ready`, `D = median(d)`, `M = median(abs(d-D))`, `Cready = median(A.ready)`, `T = max(10 ms, 0.01*Cready, 2*M)`. Timing passes only with at least 4/5 strictly faster pairs and `D > T`. A clear null/regression stops. Sole permitted extension is one five-pair block **BA, AB, BA, AB, BA** only when at least 4/5 are faster, `0.8*T <= D <= T`, and `D > max(10 ms, 0.01*Cready)`. Then decide once over all ten: at least 8/10 faster and pooled D > recomputed T. No third block, width/I/O matrix, row dropping or threshold adjustment. Inability to obtain declared valid pairs is inconclusive; integrity/cancellation failures cannot be excluded as slow rows.

Retain width-one/eight synthetic fairness checks: no new main verifier task >50 ms, heartbeat lateness ≤50 ms, CPU and withheld-read worker abort-to-rejection ≤100 ms, no ready and successful retry. For real Ghost retain matched 10 ms heartbeat/long-task/DOM progress observations: no new verifier-attributable main task >50 ms, heartbeat p95 increase ≤10 ms, ≤250 ms committed-progress gaps while bytes advance. Capture worker responsiveness/termination independently; main-isolate long tasks cannot describe worker CPU. DOM/rAF evidence proves committed progress and rendering opportunities, not painted pixels. Compare total ready as well as hash/read/queue/worker-startup timing; no clock subtraction across realms without an explicitly aligned clock. Existing verification elapsed is main-admission-to-completion, while worker read/hash durations are scalar local differences.

Only a timing pass plus integrity, resource, responsiveness, combined-memory and packed/OPFS gates supports adoption. Missing lanes remain blockers. If it loses, archive exact artifacts and stop; no automatic next worker variant. Publication and subsequent app adoption remain Root's delivery steps after qualification, not authorized by this design alone.


## Historical first independent review: corrections required and subsequently reviewed

The initial candidate passed 341 adapter tests, 1408 app tests and actual packed Chromium indexed-sparse loading, but independent Astra review reproduced lifecycle defects. No timing/adoption approval. Correct these before a fresh review:

1. Replace the worker/control Promise state machines with narrow Effect-owned control and a callback bridge whose interruption cleanup finishes before source identity-lock release. Actual sibling-failure probe currently releases the lock, disposes the operation, then terminates the worker. Preserve public error mapping and no broad scheduler framework. End the Blob/index-owning verification scope before posting reusable-slot completion; retain reply scalars only.
2. Termination failure must close the pool to new work, preserve physical capacity and failure, attempt remaining cleanup, prevent replacement dispatch, and poison/retain the resolver claim. Do not release the claim in an unconditional independent finalizer. A width-one failure currently creates a second worker; Effect finalizer failure currently still releases the claim. Cover running cancellation and preparation teardown faults.
3. Bind completion explicitly to identity, job and generation. Count bounded actual hash updates and verify exact expected read/update counts for interval-local 512 KiB reads and 64 KiB zero blocks. Map malformed protocol to the specified corrupt error; preserve I/O/deadline distinctions. Test wrong identity/digest/counts, stale messages and malformed wire data.
4. Route job/generation exhaustion through real fail-closed cleanup with a persistent close result/failure. A closed-to-new-work boolean must not skip cleanup. Test via a small internal counter seam, no public option.
5. Add the compact meaningful spec fixtures omitted from the first pass: native two-warm/two-cold width-two reservation/retained-cold/exclusive-claim test; zero-headroom/shared/custom/wrapped fallback, width-one and 10922/10923 interval boundary, consistent hints and actual derived widths; independent active/silent/mixed/tail/tampered digest/count oracles and original Blob/index/no-reopen identity; held startup/read/ack/completion abort/close/stale/retry, terminal and throwing observer, bounded progress, typed timeout/transport faults, lock/aggregate-ready/failed-termination ordering. Group cases, do not introduce a broad timing matrix.

Pinned BLAKE3 memory independently measured 131072 bytes; built worker is self-contained with no FLAC/engine loader. Existing happy-path correctness does not discharge the corrections. Engine/audio/codec/feed/pump/FLAC pool remain out of scope.

# Consumed warm-worker read-buffer disposal: one bounded follow-up

2026-09-13. Astra medium design only; no runtime edits, test or benchmark execution, release, or delegation. Required handoff: Luna xhigh implements → fresh Astra medium verifies → Root measures. Reuse `/tmp/miso-warm-worker-adapter` and `/tmp/miso-warm-worker-app`; Root synchronizes issue 96 before implementation. This amendment supersedes only the first candidate's read-buffer disposal, capability eligibility and measurement order. All worker-plan contracts and reviewed lifecycle corrections remain mandatory.

## Status and evidence

The first candidate is rejected, despite five faster pairs (ready medians 1879.0 → 1423.5 ms, paired median saving 438.7 ms, threshold 148.8 ms). Three matched memory runs found combined attributable median peaks 63,156,936 → 133,182,149 bytes: +70,025,213 against 8,388,608 allowed. Further fairness/WebKit/release gates were not run after this disqualification. Shipped adapter 0.5.2 remains the acceptance control with the original app budget.

Preserve `/tmp/miso-load-research/worker-rejected-candidate-sources.tar.gz`, rejected adapter/app patches, `worker-private-candidate.tgz` (SHA256 `b3e8afe75a8d5abe933e0c846adf4d6c77f9dd53805651a4bb3d9773a30b91cb`), dist manifest and timing/memory results. The reviewed starting tree is frozen by `worker-retained-before-review.json`; the retained proof review approved its final test correction, not qualification. Freeze follow-up artifacts under distinct names; never overwrite rejected evidence. The new runtime needs new evidence.

The selected intervention is native `ArrayBuffer.prototype.transfer(0)` for each fresh worker-local `Blob.slice(...).arrayBuffer()` result after synchronous consumption. Independent targets' roughly 64–67 MB backing-store growth followed by falls to roughly 1–3 MB supports trying explicit detachment without another forced-GC diagnostic. Detachment is an ownership operation, not a physical-RSS guarantee. No sub-second-ready claim follows.

## Small private capability boundary

Add one dependency-free private helper, for example `src/stems/sparse-verify-buffer.ts`, imported only by the warm pool and verification worker. Use a local structural type for the optional prototype method; no global declaration augmentation, dependency, polyfill, public capability API or TypeScript target/lib migration. Do not use structuredClone/message transfer as an alternative disposal implementation.

The helper obtains the current realm's prototype `transfer` method and runs one tiny semantic probe on a fresh one-byte ArrayBuffer: invoke it with receiver and new length 0; require source length 0, a zero-length ArrayBuffer result, and inability to construct a new Uint8Array over the source (detached, not merely resized). Return the verified method bound through a receiver-taking private closure, or unsupported. Use the platform method; no brittle function-source/native-code-string detection. This is feature detection, not defense against a malicious realm replacing built-ins.

Missing/non-callable capability or an unsuccessful probe is predispatch ineligibility on main. Run this within existing `SparseVerifyWorkerPool.canRun` capability selection, before creating/dispatching a verification worker or packing intervals. The admitted Blob/index then follows the existing local verifier; source width C and all admission policy remain unchanged. Avoid per-read probing: retain the verified function for the relevant pool/worker lifetime. There is no persistent capability service or negotiation message. Existing tests that replace globals must get a fresh pool/helper evaluation rather than inheriting a stale global cache.

Independently probe in the actual worker realm at validated job start, before initializing hash or reading payload. Unsupported there is an existing typed `boundary` worker failure, followed by existing failed-slot teardown; never retry locally after dispatch. Any actual payload disposal error is typed `io`, and operational construction/module/CSP/post/read/hash errors keep their current typed behavior. The benign feature probe may classify its own failure as unsupported only before dispatch; do not broadly catch the whole worker operation into fallback.

This remains a small local helper plus two call sites. Stop and report to Root if implementation requires capability negotiation, a service, engine changes or expanded public configuration.

## Ownership and synchronous consumption

Pinned `node_modules/hash-wasm/package.json` is 4.12.0. Its `lib/WASMInterface.ts:139–155` implements update by taking input subarrays, `memoryView.set(chunk)`, and calling `Hash_Update(chunk.length)` synchronously for every segment; `update` returns only after that loop. The adapter `createIncrementalBlake3` exposes that synchronous update. A fresh Blob read therefore need not retain its backing payload once update returns. Fresh review must reinspect the pinned source; this assumption is not transferable to an asynchronous/borrowing hash implementation.

In `src/internal/engine-web-sparse-verify-worker.ts`, keep disposal out of the generic zero/hash helper: that helper also receives reusable zero scratch. Only the fresh read-result owner can dispose. Never detach the admitted Blob, packed interval metadata, zero scratch, Wasm memory, shared data, stream chunks or a caller-owned/borrowed buffer. Metadata's existing transfer-to-worker remains unchanged.

Use the existing Effect callback read bridge to synchronously consume the fulfilled buffer before resuming an Effect with scalar success. This avoids an acquired ArrayBuffer sitting between an interruptible callback resume and a later cleanup registration. A narrow `readAndConsume` replacement for worker-local `readBlob` is sufficient; do not add another scheduler or public seam:

1. Keep asynchronous interval-local `slice(...).arrayBuffer()`, configured deadline, signal/listener/timer handling and exactly one outstanding read. In the promise fulfillment handler, establish local ownership immediately.
2. If the read already settled by deadline/cancellation/interruption, dispose this late result without hashing or emitting progress; retain the original settled failure. A physically terminated worker cannot execute that handler and continues to rely on platform termination, with no new claim of immediate physical reclamation.
3. For a live result, execute validation, synchronous hash consumption and disposal in one ordinary synchronous try/catch/finally region, with no Effect yield/await between ownership and disposal. Capture `readLength` before any detachment. Preserve read-wait timing at fulfillment/consumption and exact readCalls/readBytes validation. Validate short length, recheck cancellation, hash all bytes synchronously, advance canonical/hash-update counts using the captured input length, and preserve existing progress behavior. Compute/return the updated payload cursor as a scalar using readLength, never post-detach byteLength.
4. In finally, call the verified transfer function with this fresh buffer and 0, discard the zero-length result, and drop local payload/view references before resuming or launching another read. Detach on short-read, hash/progress/count/cancellation failure too, since that read result will not be used again. Keep the primary error if disposal also throws. If disposal alone fails, fail the operation as typed io and prevent ready/reuse via existing failure teardown. A late-result disposal error cannot replace a previously settled failure or cause an unhandled rejection.
5. Do not leave a detached view inside a deferred hash Effect. Extract a small synchronous body from the current `hashUpdate` if needed; the existing Effect wrapper for zero updates can delegate to it. The active read callback invokes the synchronous body directly. Keep hash duration limited to the existing hash-update work; disposal cost is included in main observed verification/ready elapsed without adding telemetry fields or cross-realm clock subtraction.

Handle the read callback's interruption finalizer by marking the read settled as well as clearing timer/listener, so a later fulfillment cannot hash after cleanup. Preserve the existing main termination-before-lock-release contract and failed-termination claim poisoning. The callback's fulfillment handler must catch all synchronous consumption/disposal exceptions into existing WorkerVerificationError values; no floating rejected promise or untyped Effect defect from newly added cleanup. Do not change the zero task checkpoint cadence or progress acknowledgement bounds.

## Frozen acceptance order and stopping rule

Root freezes new source/test/package/app/harness identities, preserving rejected artifacts. First measured gate: THREE separate matched memory runs per arm against shipped 0.5.2 with original app budget, unchanged combined main-plus-attributable-worker sampler and allowance `4 MiB + max(4 MiB, 5% of control combined peak)`. Keep complete target accounting, before/peak/teardown/reopen snapshots, no retained worker/source growth, no forced GC during measured loads, no missing-target-as-zero, no altered denominator or widened allowance. Native/browser/OPFS memory exclusions remain explicit. Missing combined attribution is unqualified, never main-only success. Failed candidate is not the acceptance control.

Only if memory passes, collect NEW five timing pairs AB, BA, AB, BA, AB with one unmeasured prime per arm and fresh per-load workers. Preserve all rows and original timing screen: d=A.ready-B.ready; D=median(d); M=median(abs(d-D)); T=max(10 ms, 1% median(A.ready), 2*M); at least 4/5 strictly faster and D>T. Sole original extension remains one reversed five-pair block only for its frozen marginal condition (4/5 faster, 0.8T≤D≤T, D>max(10 ms,1% median A)); then at least 8/10 faster and pooled D>recomputed T, no third block.

Keep Ghost eight warm stems, 845 reads, 249,323,400 active bytes, 297,980,304 canonical bytes, 1010 zero checkpoints, no warm network requests, two actual eligible verification workers and identical source widths. Preserve existing width-one/eight synthetic fairness (main verifier task/heartbeat ≤50 ms; CPU/withheld-read abort rejection ≤100 ms, no ready, clean retry), real Ghost heartbeat p95 increase ≤10 ms, no new verifier main task >50 ms, committed progress gaps ≤250 ms while bytes advance, and retained package/browser/OPFS/cancellation gates. Old timing results do not qualify changed runtime. Physical Safari/iPad remains unqualified without device evidence.

If this one candidate fails memory, timing or correctness, archive and stop this path. No automatic forced-GC investigation, worker-width variant, pool rewrite, synchronous OPFS variant or further experiment. Publication/adoption remains Root-owned after all gates; this design grants no release qualification.
